The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 e76fd7732f10b250), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 46-47. statement: Fix one source search leaf, one step in the Outgoing filters and near-band defects Lemma of [22, Section 6], and one choice in that step’s expansion of the complementary factors. In its outgoing complementary slot write xc,s = Cc,sBc,s for exactly the input-side source history left after deleting the outgoing positive filter. This inner history is shared across groups. It retains the source order, its normalized averages or identities, its O(log L) length, and the specified input-side basic Qτ s in each nonzero constituent. Write xd,s for the whole remaining source history in the other complementary slot. All endpoint evaluations use the complete inherited families, with coupled pads at compared depths, and may occur when the group is not current. Let Qc,p,s, 1 ≤ p ≤ P, be exactly that step’s individual outgoing projections, and put Qc,0,s = 0, Qc,P+1,s = 1. For a ball transfer, each Qc,p,sxc,s with 1 ≤ p ≤ P is an eligible group-indexed ball endpoint, while xc,s is shared. For a cumulative transfer the outer ball has already been removed POINTWISE CONVERGENCE OF TRIPLE AVERAGES 47 and all these endpoints are shared. The other endpoint xd,s either has its one source positive ball average outermost, with shared inner history, or is shared after that ball has been removed. Each specified eligible ball output, using its source positive average or one individual allowed pad as a singleton average, satisfies (6.6). Each specified shared output satisfies the shared conclusion of Lemma 6.1, with one union of required right-endpoint cells across its uses.
